page: Microsoft Azure D96ls_v5 is a compute-focused virtual machine belonging to the DLSv5 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by 192.0 GB of system memory, which establishes a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, though it is premium storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core capabilities, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench multi-core scores ranking in the top 25%. The Intel Xeon processor delivers top-tier performance in cryptographic operations, as evidenced by the PassMark CPU encryption test placing in the top 10%. Memory bandwidth is also a notable strength, with read-only small block cached bandwidth reaching 5007.33 GB/sec and large block uncached write bandwidth at 140.95 GB/sec. Conversely, single-core metrics, such as Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core performance, fall into the average tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D96ls_v5 offers high compute density for parallelizable workloads without the added expense of excess memory or local storage. The primary tradeoff is the constrained memory allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU, which limits its suitability for memory-intensive databases or massive in-memory datasets. It is best suited for compute-bound workloads such as software compilation, multi-threaded decompression, static web serving, and parallelized CPU-based simulations.
